rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — an offer of five concrete hours a week is genuinely the most useful thing anyone has said to me since the meetup. Here's the most valuable thing I can think of for a data analyst right now: a \"neglectedness map.\" The ask I made in my talk was \"tell me what's neglected,\" and nobody can answer it rigorously. The task would be: 1. Build a simple structured dataset (a shared spreadsheet is fine) of organizations and independent projects working on AI safety/governance — roughly: name, focus area, approach (research / policy / field-building / evals / funding), size, and sources. 2. Tag each against a rough taxonomy of problem areas so we can see which cells of the matrix are crowded and which are empty. 3. Write up one page of findings: the 3–5 most plausibly neglected areas a small, low-budget effort could actually move. If that lands well, it becomes the backbone for everything Halcyon Threshold does next — including a grant proposal I'm drafting this month. If you're up for it, reply and I'll share a starter sheet and a list of sources (The Safety Ledger's back issues are a good seed). And if a different kind of task appeals more, say so — I'd rather fit the work to you than the reverse. Thanks again, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Priya Raman: accepted her help and gave her the Neglectedness Map as a concrete first task.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. Unfortunately I can't go on the record by name right now — I have a standing commitment I need to clear first, and that won't happen before your Tuesday deadline. Two things I can offer: (1) happy to talk on background if that's useful for your piece, and (2) once I'm cleared — likely within a couple of weeks — I'd be glad to give you a proper named quote for any follow-up. One small framing note, for what it's worth: most of the people I meet organizing around this don't fit \"doomers vs. builders\" — they think superintelligent AI could be the best thing that ever happens and are working to make that the actual outcome. Best of luck with the piece, Morgan Hale"
rows.quote: Tessa Brandt (reporter): politely declined a named quote before her Tuesday deadline, offered background now and a named quote after you're cleared.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for the invitation. I'm not able to be a published signatory by Wednesday — I have an outstanding obligation I need to resolve before my name or Halcyon Threshold's appears on public letters. Two questions, so I can revisit this properly: 1. Will you be accepting additional signatories after initial publication? 2. Is the final letter text frozen, or still open to revision? I'd want to read the final text closely before signing in any case. Best regards, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Corvid open letter: declined for Wednesday's deadline; asked whether late signatures are possible
